title: Göktürk Khaganate
capsule: The First Turkic Khaganate (Göktürk Khaganate) was founded by Bumin Qaghan of the Ashina clan, who revolted against the Rouran in 552 and rapidly built a steppe empire stretching from Manchuria to the Black Sea; the dataset records it from 555 to 586. Bumin died within a year of his triumph and the empire was divided between his son Muqan Qaghan in the east and brother Istemi Qaghan in the west, the latter opening direct diplomatic and commercial relations with Byzantium and Sasanian Iran. The khaganate was the first Central Asian power to create a formal runic script (Old Turkic), attested in the Orkhon inscriptions. Internal strife and Chinese Sui manipulation led to the khaganate's splitting into distinct Eastern and Western Göktürk polities by c. 581–603.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Göktürk territorial extent is reconstructed from Chinese annals (Suishu, Beishi) and Byzantine diplomatic records; the empire's enormous steppe span makes precise boundaries highly conjectural, with only core pasture zones and key garrison points reliably identified.
